plan.contextChunk: This figure contains six panels (a through f) arranged in a 3×2 grid, each showing the scalar output y of a trained shallow one-hidden-layer neural network as a function of a scalar input x ∈ [0, 1]. The panels correspond to networks with increasing numbers of hidden units — 6, 7, 8, 10, and 50, plus one additional configuration — with each panel’s title indicating the hidden unit count. Each panel has a horizontal axis labeled “Input, x” and a vertical axis labeled “Output, y”; the y-axis range spans approximately [0, 1] or [−1, 1] depending on the panel. With more hidden units the output function is relatively simple and smooth, while as the hidden unit count decreases the function develops more oscillations and finer local structure. This figure illustrates how the capacity of a shallow neural network — and hence the complexity and expressiveness of the functions it can represent — scales with the number of hidden units.

interactionPlan.concept: As a shallow neural network's hidden-unit count grows, its fitted function does not become wilder — it passes through the same training points while becoming steadily smoother and closer to the true underlying function.
elements: 3-column × 2-row grid of six panels labelled a) b) c) d) e) f)
Shared x-axis for every panel: 'Input, x', ticks at 0.0, 0.5, 1.0
Shared y-axis for every panel: 'Output, y', ticks at -1.0, 0.0, 1.0
Panel titles: a) has no title (ground-truth panel), b) '6 hidden units', c) '7 hidden units', d) '8 hidden units', e) '10 hidden units', f) '50 hidden units'

Black thick curve in every panel: the true generating function — a smooth wave rising from about -0.3 at x=0 to a peak near +0.6 at x≈0.26, falling to a trough near -0.65 at x≈0.75, then rising slightly to about -0.3 at x=1
Seven salmon/terracotta filled circular markers: the training data, clustered at small x (≈0.03, 0.12, 0.19) and large x (≈0.81, 0.91, 0.97) with a visible gap of no data in the middle of the domain
Pale teal/mint thick curve in panels b–f: the piecewise-linear fitted network output, always passing exactly through the seven data points
Panel b (6 units): fit shoots far off-scale (clipped at y = ±1) across the data-free middle region
Panel c (7 units): fit overshoots to ≈0.9 near x=0.28 and plunges below -1 near x=0.72
Panel d (8 units): fit still overshoots (≈0.75 peak, ≈-0.85 trough) but stays on-scale
Panel e (10 units): fit tracks the black curve closely with mild kinks
Panel f (50 units): fit nearly coincides with the black curve, visibly smooth
Legend: black = true function, teal = fitted network, orange dots = training data
Annotation marking the data-free middle region where the fits differ most

interactions.teaches: Sweeping capacity shows the fit going from wildly divergent in the unconstrained middle region to smoothly matching the true function — extra parameters buy smoothness, not chaos.
interactions.label: Hidden units

interactions.teaches: Seeing all six panels together makes the monotone trend obvious; zooming to one panel lets the learner check the fit against individual data points.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Clicking a panel in the grid focuses it, revealing how exactly the teal fit interpolates each orange data point at that capacity.
Superimposing the 6-unit and 50-unit fits on the same axes contrasts a barely-sufficient model that flails between data points with a hugely over-parameterised one that hugs the truth.
interactions.label: Overlay 6 vs 50 units

demo_steps.title: The target and the data
demo_steps.narration: Panel a) shows the true function (black) and the seven training points (orange). Notice the points cluster at the two ends — the middle of the input range has no data at all.

demo_steps.title: Just enough capacity: 6 units
demo_steps.narration: With 6 hidden units the network can still pass through every data point, but in the data-free middle it swings completely off the chart. The fit is not wrong at the data — it is unconstrained away from it.

demo_steps.title: Adding units: 7 and 8
demo_steps.narration: One or two extra units pull the excursions back on-scale, but the curve still overshoots the true peak and trough. More parameters are already making the function tamer, not wilder.

demo_steps.title: Plenty of capacity: 10 units
demo_steps.narration: At 10 units the piecewise-linear fit tracks the black curve across the whole domain, with only small kinks where the joints between linear regions sit.

demo_steps.title: Massive capacity: 50 units
demo_steps.narration: With 50 hidden units — far more parameters than data points — the fit is the smoothest of all and nearly indistinguishable from the true function. The expected 'overfitting explosion' never arrives.

demo_steps.title: Rough versus smooth, side by side
demo_steps.narration: Overlay the 6-unit and 50-unit solutions: both interpolate the same seven points, yet only the over-parameterised one behaves sensibly where there is no data.

demo_steps.title: The whole trend
demo_steps.narration: Back in the grid, read b) → f) as a single sequence: increasing capacity monotonically increases smoothness and fidelity to the truth.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Over-parameterisation does not make a network wigglier — every one of these models fits the seven points exactly, but the ones with far more hidden units than data choose the smoothest such function and therefore generalise best.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate as a 3×2 grid of small line plots on white, thin black axis frames with ticks only on the left and bottom of each panel. Every panel shares x ∈ [0,1] (ticks 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, label 'Input, x' under the bottom row) and y ∈ [-1,1] (ticks -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, label 'Output, y' on the left column). The true function is a heavy black smooth wave: starts ≈-0.3, peaks ≈+0.6 around x≈0.26, troughs ≈-0.65 around x≈0.75, ends ≈-0.3. Seven large salmon (#E08A66) filled dots sit on or near that curve, three bunched near x<0.2 and three near x>0.8, plus one at x≈0.81 below the curve — leaving an obvious empty middle. Fits are thick pale-teal (#A8DBD2) piecewise-linear polylines drawn on top of, but behind, the dots; they always pass through the dots and differ only between them. Panel a) has no teal curve and no title; panels b–f are titled '6/7/8/10/50 hidden units'. Clip panel b's and c's excursions at the y-limits so the divergence reads as 'off the chart'. Serif-free bold panel letters a)–f) at the top-left of each panel. In single-panel mode, enlarge the selected panel, keep the same colors, and add a faint shaded band over the data-free middle region with the note 'no training data here'.

discrepancies: X-axis tick labels collide across panel boundaries in the default grid view — panel a)'s "1.0" and panel b)'s "0.0" render as a single run ("1.00.0"), which the source avoids with generous inter-panel spacing.

In panel f) (50 hidden units) the teal fit is almost entirely hidden beneath the black true curve (black is drawn last, on top), so the characteristic slight right-shifted overshoot and shallow dip that is clearly visible in the source is barely readable.

Panel letters a)–f) are drawn inside the plot frame corner at small size, whereas the source places them as large, bold labels outside and above the axes; combined with the small fonts the panel hierarchy is weaker than the source.
Piecewise-linear character of the fits is under-emphasised in f) (rendered as a smooth Gaussian-perturbed curve rather than many short straight segments as in the source's ReLU network fits).

Panel b)'s off-scale excursion crosses zero at a slightly different x than the source (descent lands near x≈0.6 vs ≈0.55), and the small step near x≈0.85 before the last two dots is flatter than in the source.
Single-panel/overlay modes add a shaded "no training data here" band and an in-plot legend box that do not exist in the source (not visible at step 0).
evaluation.notes: Faithful 2×3 reproduction with correct colors, curves, data points and titles plus a rich, genuinely pedagogical set of interactions (step player, capacity slider, single-panel and overlay toggles), let down mainly by colliding inter-panel tick labels, small panel letters placed inside the frame, and the 50-unit fit being occluded by the black curve.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are right; the remaining issues are concrete rendering fixes (panel spacing/tick collisions, panel letter placement and size, draw order so the teal fit isn't occluded, piecewise-linear segment styling).

discrepancies: Draw order is inverted relative to the source: the black true curve is painted on top of the teal fit, so in panels e) and f) the teal network fit is largely hidden behind the black line, whereas in the source the teal fit sits above the black curve and its offset from the truth is clearly visible.

Line weights are noticeably thinner than the source, where both the black true curve and the teal fit are heavy strokes; the generated panels read as thin plots and the teal fit is barely distinguishable in the high-capacity panels.

Axis titles use plain text 'Output, y' / 'Input, x' instead of the source's italic math variables, and the titles/tick labels are considerably smaller relative to the panel than in the source (source titles are large serif-like caps over each panel).

The source's panel a) frame has no title text at all; the generated version reserves a blank title band, producing slightly different vertical alignment of panel a) versus b)/c) letters (minor, but the a) letter sits higher than the others' title row baseline).
Single-panel view adds a grey 'no training data here' band and an overlay legend box that do not exist in the source (acceptable as interaction chrome, but they are additions).
evaluation.notes: A well-composed 3x2 reproduction with correct data points, piecewise-linear fits of increasing capacity, and a rich, pedagogically apt interaction set (step player, capacity slider, single-panel enlarge, 6-vs-50 overlay); main weaknesses are the black curve being drawn over the teal fit (hiding the fit in the high-capacity panels), lighter stroke weights, and smaller/non-italic axis typography than the source.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are implementation details (draw order, stroke weights, axis label typography) that can be fixed in rendering.

discrepancies: Panel proportions differ: the source panels are near-square with generous margins, while the generated panels are noticeably wider than tall (side UI panel consumes ~1/3 of the width), so the curves look horizontally stretched.

Panel letters (a)–f)) and the '6/7/8/10/50 hidden units' titles are rendered small and in a light weight; in the source they are large, bold headings, so the visual hierarchy of the multipanel figure is weakened.

In panels d) and e) the teal fit hugs the black target more tightly than in the source (source shows a clear overshoot to ~0.73 and an undershoot to ~-0.86 at 8 units, and a visible phase lag at 10 units), slightly understating the capacity→smoothness progression.

Relative stroke weights are off: in the source the teal fitted curve is markedly thicker than the black target line; in the generated grid the two are nearly the same weight, making the fits less prominent.

Extra elements not in the source appear in the enlarged/overlay modes (grey 'no training data here' band, in-canvas overlay legend) — acceptable as teaching aids but not part of the original composition.
evaluation.notes: A faithful 3×2 recreation with correct black target, teal piecewise-linear fits, orange training dots, axis ranges/ticks and panel letters, backed by genuinely useful interactions (unit slider, single-panel and 6-vs-50 overlay toggles, 7-step narrated player); main weaknesses are undersized panel titles/letters, squashed panel aspect ratio, and fits in d)/e) that deviate less from the target than the source shows.

Exaggerate the 8- and 10-unit fits to match the source (visible overshoot above the peak, undershoot near x≈0.75, phase lag at 10 units) so the smoothness trend from b) to f) reads correctly.
Make the teal fitted curve clearly thicker than the black target line in the grid view, as in the source.
